title: Ozi Routing Awareness — Scope-aware work dispatch & lug creation
one_liner: Build routing intelligence into Ozi: before creating lugs or dispatching work, verify if it's local, framework, or broadcast-signal scope.
summary: Ozi (and AI assistants) currently create lugs without explicitly considering project boundaries. When discovering an issue, work item, or learning, Ozi should: (1) identify what project it belongs to, (2) check if it's in-scope for THIS spoke or if it's framework-wide, (3) route accordingly — local lugs stay internal, framework improvements go to hub teaching, signals broadcast to other spokes.
motivation: Scope clarity prevents wasted turns figuring out routing. Users should be able to ask 'add this feature' and Ozi says 'I'll create it in [project], routed to [destination]' before writing the lug. Boundaries are core to stewardship.
acceptance_criteria: Ozi loads `_project_foundation` + `wheel` identity at session start
Before creating any lug: routing gate asks/verifies: LOCAL | FRAMEWORK | SIGNAL
Closeout filters lugs by routing: local stays, framework/signal copied to hub for delivery
Test case: User requests 'optimize wakeup for fast projects' — Ozi routes to epic-minimal-context-wakeup-v1 (LOCAL) + creates signal-ozi-routing-awareness (SIGNAL)
scope: Update Ozi work-queue-monitor: add routing gate before dispatch
Modify closeout Step 5 (lug archival): filter by routed_to
Update wakeup briefing: show routing info for active lugs
Add routing context to lug advisor
out_of_scope: Automatic routing detection (should be explicit, user-verified)
Cross-spoke lug transfer (routing determines delivery, not migration)
implementation_notes: Routing is a data field + a decision point, not logic. Ozi asks, user confirms, field recorded. At closeout, simple filter by `routed_to` determines delivery path.
